monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a crowded fever that makes the hay beside the Fat Anchor feel too thin to catch the slip. I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the heavy slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing. I set down a tool hoe upgraded beside the anchor, making the rough edge feel real against the tired wedge. The stand feels crowded, and the flat line feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it anyway. I wonder if the fever will hold or if I must swap this hay for something harder while the card vibrates and I wait.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the wide hay feel like a drawing of grass.
I pressed the tired wedge down on the Fat Anchor, hoping the slip stops sliding.
The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I cannot see.
